design.plan_section: docs/EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md, '2026-08-01 Phase 1B 推理期接触引导 P2（协议对齐，用户批准）'
design.question: HOIPrior's fixed native protocol samples 500 unguided steps while every baseline it has been compared against was sampled with inference-time contact guidance. Does aligning the protocol - applying the author's complete apply_hoi_guidance_loss to the sealed D2-X checkpoint at inference - close the recorded contact gap, and at what cost?
design.framing: protocol alignment, NOT a model improvement: it changes how HOIPrior is sampled, not the quality of the prior, and cannot change the 0.83 cm [0.49, 1.18] genuine generative-geometry deficit measured on 2026-08-01
design.manipulated_factor: inference-time guidance configuration only (arm, guidance_scale, step schedule, clamping)
design.invariant: the same sealed D2-X checkpoint, the same official 438-sequence three-window 500-step native protocol, byte-identical metric code

arms.A: InfBaGel-faithful port: full loss, guidance_scale 1.0, gradient taken w.r.t. x0_hat and added raw to x_{t-1}, guided on every reverse step except the last
arms.B: CHOIS-style DDPM analogue: last 10 reverse steps only, gradient scaled by posterior_variance[t] and the resulting update clamped to +-1.0, guidance_scale 1000.0 (the cited classifier_scale = 1e3); at scale 1.0 the variance scaling would shrink the update by about 3.8e-4 and Arm B would have been an accidental null arm

design.loss: code/guidance_loss.py:88-94 apply_hoi_guidance_loss = hand-object x10 PLUS feet-floor x500; the feet-floor term is exactly what D2-Q0 and D2-R0 omitted
design.target_checkpoint_rationale: D2-X, not D2-AG: D2-AG's self-conditioned relation source consumes `current` (code/priors/diffusion.py:234-236) and guidance modifies `current`, which would be an uncontrolled distribution shift

gt_leakage_audit.gt_contact_use: GT contact annotation enters only as the two window-0 seed history frames, identically in the unguided path
gt_leakage_audit.author_cross_check: CHOIS's GT contact_labels argument is shadowed and never read (chois_release/manip/model/trainer_chois.py:2024)

design.lifecycle_profile: user-approved inference-only measurement under the lean HOIPrior workflow: no run id allocated and no tools/experiment.py start manifest; traceability rests on the executed git commit, the archived Hydra config and overrides, the fixed official 438-sequence test set and byte-identical metric code

executed_commits.closure_commit_note: the dated plan results, this compact result, the phase summary, the evidence-index row and the registry completion row are one closure change; the executed source object above predates it

source_hashes.contact_guidance_py_note: the sealed D2-Q0 partial implementation, deliberately left untouched so that the historical diagnostic is not retroactively changed

declared_confounds.subject: guidance consumes geometry the model never sees
declared_confounds.detail: the guidance loss uses the full posed object mesh (13,086-38,353 vertices) while HOIPrior conditions only on a 1024-point BPS. That mesh is already used by the evaluator, but it is extra test-time geometry the model itself never receives, so part of the gain is purchased with information outside the prior.

declared_confounds.subject: the foot-sliding improvement may be partly metric-shaped
declared_confounds.detail: the FS metric estimates the floor from the PREDICTED joints (code/test_infbagel_hoi.py:249, code/eval_metrics.py:101-113) while the guidance pins the support foot to a fixed 0.02 m. The two can be mutually self-consistent, so Arm B's FS ratio 0.9797 must not be read as a pure physical-plausibility gain.

declared_confounds.subject: determinism convention
declared_confounds.detail: the deterministic vertex subset of D2-Q0 is used instead of the author's torch.randperm(...)[:10000] (code/models/infbagel.py:736), so the same configuration reproduces; this differs from the author's implementation.

armA.role: preregistered primary arm; InfBaGel-faithful port of the author's full guidance

guidance.note: last_steps and clamp are read for both arms but only take effect for arm b (code/priors/inference_guidance.py:133-140,371-381); arm a guides every reverse step except the final one

armB.role: preregistered declared second arm; CHOIS-style DDPM analogue

guidance.note: last_steps and clamp are read for both arms but only take effect for arm b (code/priors/inference_guidance.py:133-140,371-381); arm a guides every reverse step except the final one

control_d2x.role: unguided control: sealed D2-X checkpoint under the fixed native protocol, bit-exact local reproduction of the sealed worker evaluation

reference_a0_old.role: guided released InfBaGel under its own published protocol; the parity reference. Baseline only, never an initializer.
reference_a0_old.distance_source_note: the distance statistics come from the -ps- determinism replicate, whose 18 aggregate metrics are bit-identical to a0-old

ctrl.role: unguided control on the identical 4-sequence subset

gate.scope: runnability and finiteness only; explicitly not used to choose between arms
gate.plan_reference: docs/EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md, P2 section: '功能性 smoke 仅检验可运行性与有限性（nonfinite_values == 0 为被门控项），不用于在两臂之间做选择'
gate.note: the four-sequence subset is not a scientific comparison; its contact numbers are not comparable to the official 438 and are recorded only for completeness

extraction_gate.purpose: recompute per-sequence contact statistics independently of the aggregates before any contrast is formed

ground_truth_reference.note: identical for all eight runs; it is the GT-vs-GT floor of the metric

gt_contact_distance.definition: per GT-contact frame, min over the two SMPL hand joints (22, 23) of the distance to the nearest vertex of the posed predicted object mesh; restricted to frames where either GT hand is within the 5 cm contact threshold, i.e. the mask at code/eval_metrics.py:271
gt_contact_distance.measurement_caveat: FROM a skeleton hand joint, not the hand mesh surface, and TO the nearest object mesh vertex, not the nearest surface point; both the prediction and the GT leg use the identical definition

gain_shares.form: Arm B's paired gain over the unguided control divided by Arm A's, on the same quantity; both gains have CIs excluding zero except where noted
gain_shares.statement: Arm B retains about 88% of Arm A's contact-recall gain, 96% of its contact-F1 gain, 85% of its predicted-contact gain and 85% of its distance gain, at a near-zero object-trajectory cost and with foot sliding improved rather than degraded. The plan's '~90% of the contact gain, ~85% of the distance gain' refers to these ratios.

criteria.statement: P2 preregistered mandatory cost REPORTING but preregistered no cost THRESHOLD. D2-Q0's <=1.10 protection bar was preregistered for D2-Q0 and is not P2's gate. No pass or fail against that line is declared here. It is evaluated below only for comparability with the earlier sub-phases, not as a P2 verdict.

d2q0_style_ratio_bar.bar: mean-ratio 95% CI upper bound <= 1.10 against the unguided control

armA.verdict_if_applied: would FAIL on foot sliding (CI upper 1.166076707633881) and would clear object translation by 0.000168516

criteria.arm_reporting_rule: Arm A is the preregistered headline and is reported as such regardless of outcome; Arm B was declared before any run and is reported on equal terms. The primary-arm declaration is not rewritten because Arm B looks better on cost.

recorded_in: docs/EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md, P2 section, '事前预测（在任何 GPU 运行之前记录）'
pre_run_prediction.prediction: Arm A was predicted to raise position_outside_rate and possibly produce degenerate motion, because with a real norm.npy one guidance step adds about 2.06 to the [-1,1] normalized pelvis-y channel at 5 cm foot error and about 19 at 30 cm, and HOIPrior applies the raw gradient on 499 steps where the author applies it on 15.
pre_run_prediction.likely_reason: the worst case did not materialise, most likely because the loss falls towards zero once contact is achieved, so the guidance is self-limiting: Arm A's mean gradient RMS is 0.1525 while its max absolute value is 437.9, i.e. large updates are rare and transient rather than sustained.

nan_risk_inherited_from_author.description: the temporal term computes v/||v|| with no epsilon (code/guidance_loss.py:58-64), which is NaN when the palm sits exactly at the object centre

end_obj_trans_err_construction.issue: the per-sequence construction and the published aggregate are not the same quantity: the aggregate uses the pre-interpolation window endpoint, the per-sequence value uses the final frame of the interpolated trajectory
end_obj_trans_err_construction.consequence: the end_obj_trans_err CIs in this file are per-sequence-construction CIs, not CIs on the published aggregate

mpjpe_pooling.issue: pooling order differs between the per-sequence mean and the aggregate

penetration_sequence_count.reason: the frozen metric code does not compute the penetration terms for six object classes, so both penetration CIs rest on 181 sequences

contact_recall_scoring_artifact.note: unchanged by P2; it affects every recall in this project equally and does not affect any P2 contrast, all of which are paired on the same 438 sequences

contact_parity_with_the_guided_released_.statement: protocol-aligned, the guided HOIPrior reaches statistical contact parity with the guided released model

geometry_moved_not_only_the_operating_po.statement: the whole distribution moved, which no rethresholding can produce; and on the unthresholded residual Arm A is indistinguishable from the guided released model, so parity holds off the threshold as well

d2q0_negative_overturned.d2q0_implementation_defect: code/priors/contact_guidance.py (D2-Q0) and code/priors/routed_guidance.py (D2-R0) reference apply_feet_floor_contact_guidance zero times; both implemented only the hand-object x10 term and omitted the feet-floor x500 term
d2q0_negative_overturned.statement: with the author's complete loss, Arm B's foot-sliding ratio is 0.9797, an improvement, and Arm A's is 1.0992; the D2-Q0 foot-sliding cost was a property of a partial implementation measured on a far weaker checkpoint

residual_deficit_guidance_does_not_fix.statement: Arm A's >=8 cm tail stays fatter than the released model's (0.1272 vs 0.1052) and object-trajectory and penetration costs remain against a0-old. That is consistent with the 0.83 cm [0.49, 1.18] genuine generative-geometry gap measured on 2026-08-01: the contact failure was a measurement artifact, the remaining gaps are real.

conclusion: Aligning HOIPrior's inference protocol with the protocol its baselines were measured under closes the recorded contact gap. Guided, the sealed D2-X checkpoint reaches statistical contact parity with the guided released model: Arm A minus a0-old has contact recall -0.0043, precision +0.0114, F1 +0.0035 and contact_percent -0.0120, all four with CIs crossing zero, and Arm B's F1 difference -0.0007 also crosses zero. The gain is geometric, not a shift of operating point: the paired GT-contact-frame distance moves -1.4371 cm [-1.7204, -1.1532], the median goes 3.1835 -> 1.7178 cm, the [0,2) cm mass rises 0.359 -> 0.547, and on the unthresholded residual Arm A is indistinguishable from the guided released model (+0.2216 cm, CI crosses zero). Arm A is the preregistered primary and has the highest contact F1 (0.73071), but Arm B is the configuration that survives cost scrutiny: about 88% of the recall gain, 96% of the F1 gain and 85% of the distance gain, with an object-translation ratio of 1.0063 and foot sliding IMPROVED at 0.9797. P2 preregistered mandatory cost reporting but no cost threshold; reported only for comparability, if D2-Q0's <=1.10 bar were applied Arm A would fail foot sliding (CI upper 1.1661) and clear object translation by 1.7e-4, while Arm B would clear both. D2-Q0's negative is overturned: it omitted the feet-floor term entirely and measured on a checkpoint with 95.3 cm object-goal error. The pre-run prediction that Arm A would saturate position_outside_rate and degenerate is FALSIFIED - every run has nonfinite_values 0 and position_outside_rate 0.0. What guidance does not fix: Arm A's >=8 cm tail is still fatter than the released model's (0.1272 vs 0.1052) and object-trajectory and penetration costs remain against a0-old, consistent with the 0.83 cm genuine generative-geometry gap. This is protocol alignment, not a model improvement: it changes how HOIPrior is sampled, not the quality of the prior.
next_action: Treat every historical released-minus-D2 contact comparison as protocol-confounded on the guidance axis as well, and cite this result when a HOIPrior contact number is compared with a guided baseline. This sub-phase trains nothing, selects no checkpoint, changes neither the evaluator nor the fixed native D2 protocol, and does not enable guidance in production: guidance remains default-off and any production use, any stepwise object requery, and any use of these runs as a checkpoint-selection signal still require a separate dated plan amendment and explicit user approval. Phase 1B HOIPrior search remains closed and the next session entry point is unchanged: a dated Phase 1C HSIPrior plan-only preregistration on phase/01c-hsi, trained from random initialization.
